## Dataset

### Outlet coverage

```{r outlet-coverage}
coverage |>
  left_join(
    scores |>
      group_by(source_domain) |>
      summarise(avg_words = round(mean(word_count)),
                first = min(published_date), last = max(published_date), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "source_domain"
  ) |>
  arrange(country, desc(final_articles)) |>
  select(country, outlet_name, gdelt_urls, final_articles, avg_words, first, last) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Country", "Outlet", "GDELT URLs", "Final articles", "Avg words",
                  "First seen", "Last seen"),
    caption = "All 51 queried outlets: URLs returned by GDELT (outlet's own site only) and articles in the final sample"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) |>
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top") |>
  scroll_box(height = "420px")
```

`r n_outlets_zero` of the 51 outlets returned no URLs at all, among them the Washington Post,
the Wall Street Journal and the Times of Israel. Zero matching articles in three months of
this war is implausible for outlets of that size. The original collector treated rate-limited or failed GDELT
requests as empty results; the corrected collector logs them, but this window was not
re-collected. Le Monde returned 130 URLs, all of them JavaScript walls with no article text.

### From GDELT hits to the final sample

```{r attrition}
attrition |>
  mutate(kept = percent(language_ok / gdelt, accuracy = 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(language_ok)) |>
  kbl(
    col.names = c("Country", "GDELT URLs", "Own site", "Scraped", "≥ 100 words",
                  "Deduplicated", "Final", "Kept"),
    caption = "Articles remaining after each pipeline step"
  ) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"))
```

The *own site* step removes `r sum(attrition$gdelt - attrition$right_site)` URLs that GDELT
returned for the wrong outlet: its `domain:` filter matches suffixes, so local London papers
came back as *The Independent* and Tagesspiegel as *Der Spiegel*, which is left with no articles.
The other large losses are blocked pages (Canada, Le Monde), the same story under several
URLs (CNN, Jerusalem Post) and pages in another language (CNN Arabic, El País in English).

### Articles per country

```{r country-bar, fig.height=4.5}
scores |>
  count(country) |>
  left_join(coverage |> filter(final_articles > 0) |> count(country, name = "outlets"),
            by = "country") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(country, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4472C4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(comma(n), "  (", outlets, " outlet", ifelse(outlets > 1, "s", ""), ")")),
            hjust = -0.05, size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Articles per country in the final sample", x = "Articles", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

The UK and Israel supply `r percent(mean(scores$country %in% c("UK", "Israel")), accuracy = 1)`
of the sample, so pooled figures lean towards them. Canada rests on a single outlet, and
Spain, Argentina and Brazil are too small for country-level conclusions; Brazil is left out
of the country charts below (minimum `r MIN_COUNTRY_N` articles).

### Weekly coverage

```{r weekly, fig.height=4}
scores |>
  count(week) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4472C4") +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 weeks", date_labels = "%d %b") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Articles per week, all sources",
       subtitle = "Weeks start on Monday; date = day GDELT first saw the article",
       x = NULL, y = "Articles") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

Coverage is thin until mid-February, jumps in the week of 23 February and peaks in the week
of 2 March (`r max(count(scores, week)$n)` articles), when English headlines are dominated by
*strikes*, *Tehran* and *Lebanon*; from mid-March they add *oil*, *Gulf* and *Hormuz*.
`r percent(mean(scores$published_date >= as.Date("2026-02-23")), accuracy = 1)` of the
articles date from 23 February onwards, so the pooled results mostly describe that phase.
